why_trail.why: Baseline loaded. Key map facts conditioning the plan: (1) grip production path does NOT exclude rain sessions - grip_batch stores every session and grip_baseline inflates session_offset_sigma by a flat RAIN_SIGMA_INFLATION=4.0; the 20-of-36 weekend drop lived in the uncommitted #678 spike's candidate selection, so the issue's premise is misattributed to grip_baseline. (2) An identical wet-exclusion problem is already SOLVED and map-documented in the fuel subsystem: burn_rate_calibration.session_wet_fraction reads the stored session_surface_features.wet_lap_fraction with a named WET_EXCLUDE_THRESHOLD=0.05 - a precedented physics-to-data read (physics.md L143-161). (3) That seam is populated for session_type='R' ONLY (probe: 0 non-race sessions carry wet_lap_fraction in 2022-2025), which is exactly the coverage the grip fit needs.

Problem statement reframed by evidence, not accepted from the issue text. The issue attributes an over-aggressive rain EXCLUSION to grip_baseline; the code has no exclusion at all -- it stores every session and applies a flat 4x sigma inflation, and the 20-of-36 drop lived in the uncommitted #678 spike. The real defect is the absence of a production selection predicate plus the absence of any graded wet signal for non-race sessions. The issue's own first-named remedy (a fraction-of-wet-SAMPLES threshold) is measurably wrong in both directions on 2022-2024 data; the discriminating instrument is the WET/INTERMEDIATE lap fraction, which this repo already uses under a named threshold in the fuel subsystem but populates for races only. Residual hazard the threshold alone cannot cover: a mixed session's surviving DRY laps sit on a DRYING track, which violates the monotone-rubber-in model directly.

Plan frozen at 7 crew gates over 14 files. The shape follows from three measured facts rather than from the issue text: (1) production has no rain exclusion, so the deliverable is a graded signal plus ONE named selection predicate, not a loosened filter; (2) the issue's own first-named remedy (wet-sample fraction) is wrong in both directions on real data, so the instrument is the stored WET/INTERMEDIATE lap fraction -- already precedented and map-sanctioned in the fuel subsystem, but populated for races only, which makes the data-layer coverage gate load-bearing rather than optional; (3) a threshold alone cannot honor the acceptance clause about the monotone-grip assumption, because a recovered mixed session's surviving DRY laps sit on a DRYING track -- hence the drying-window guard as its own gate. Two rigor mechanisms ran with recorded form deviations (no subagents available): plan-alternatives converged to one recommendation, and an adversarial self-critique changed the plan in seven places -- most importantly making a pre-re-batch snapshot mandatory, since force=True overwrites the grip store irreversibly and would otherwise have destroyed the before half of the required held-out comparison. A genuine cold critic remains owed and is wired as e0-context.c2.
